date_note: Date of Elliptic's update of 23 November; the page was first published on 3 November and says it was last updated on 23 November.
title: Elliptic: at least 3,930 BTC ($247 million) from the Binance theft has gone into coinjoins since November 1
summary: Elliptic's 23 November update says at least 3,930 BTC ($247 million) of the funds stolen from Binance has gone into coinjoins since November 1. It says it tracks more than 27,000 wallets on at least 16 blockchains, about 55 services and about 90,000 transactions, and that those laundered may be with Chinese money laundering networks. Elliptic says the laundering is clearly automated but nothing it has seen shows an AI agent making decisions.
plain: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic says at least 3,930 BTC ($247 million) of the money stolen from Binance has been put through mixing transactions, and that the funds may be with Chinese laundering networks.
exec: Elliptic reports at least 3,930 BTC ($247 million) of Binance theft proceeds has been mixed since November 1, which complicates tracing and recovery.

evidence.quote: At least 3,930 BTC ($247 million) has now gone into coinjoins since November 1.

validation.note: Elliptic's own report is the primary source; Bitcoin.com News (Jamie Redman, 23 Nov) relays it and adds Elliptic co-founder Tom Robinson's LinkedIn remark that the China link is not conclusive. The PANews item cites CoinDesk, which was not read.
